name: Knack
subcategory: spreadsheet databases and operational data apps
tagline: Build a small hosted database app with pages, forms, and role-based views

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: 20,000 records; 3 apps; 2 GB storage; 25 AI credits; 500 Flows transactions; 1,000 API calls/day; 1 shared builder.
tiers.notes: Current new-customer promotion advertises $19/month for the first 3 months, then the regular price.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 50,000 records; unlimited apps; 10 GB storage; 1-month history; 50 AI credits; 2,000 Flows transactions; 5,000 API calls/day.
tiers.notes: Current new-customer promotion advertises $49/month for the first 3 months. Advanced SSO is a $55/month add-on.

tiers.name: Corporate
tiers.limits: Starts with 125,000 records and scales to 2.5 million; 50 GB storage; 2-month history; 100 AI credits; 5,000 Flows transactions; 10,000 API calls/day.
tiers.notes: Published price is a starting price and rises with capacity.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: 2.5 million+ records; 3-month logs; custom storage, API and usage limits.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no permanent free tier; free trial offered with no card, but the live pricing page does not state its duration
pricing.billingTerms: monthly month-to-month + annual; annual rates are about 17% lower and billed for the year
pricing.hiddenCosts: Record/storage add-ons cost $42/month for 15,000 records + 5 GB on Pro (maximum 2) or $90/month for 40,000 records + 20 GB on Corporate (maximum 2); Pro SSO is $55/month; paid plans can auto-add Flows capacity at unpublished prices; each app user consumes a database record.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Knack, build a small hosted database app with pages, forms, and role-based views. The hard boundary is managed hosting, schema builder, permissions, integrations, and support, plus data model flexibility, collaboration, and integrations.
coreLoopDIY: Model structured records in a small self-hosted database app, provide grid, form, kanban, and role-based filtered views, and expose a documented API.
whatYouLose: managed hosting, schema builder, permissions, integrations, and support
moatNotes: data model flexibility, collaboration, and integrations
ongoingBurden: schema changes, formulas, permissions, imports, attachments, views, APIs, concurrency, backups, and migrations
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Knack because teams pay when a flexible database becomes a shared operational system with integrations and years of accumulated business logic. The recurring cost buys schema changes, formulas, permissions, imports, attachments, views, APIs, concurrency, backups, and migrations, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: NocoDB
priorArt.desc: Active open-source no-code database interface and Airtable alternative.

alternatives.name: Baserow Free
alternatives.desc: Its free app builder turns tables into pages and forms for hundreds of external users, with basic roles and automations.

facts.dataFormat: Tables, application definitions, uploads, and workspace metadata live in Baserow Cloud; tables can be exported as CSV
facts.gapVsPaid: Its app builder is less polished for customer-facing portals and offers shallower external-user permissions and page composition than Knack.

alternatives.name: Budibase
alternatives.desc: Internal apps, forms, automations, and portals in one box; much closer to Knack than its developer branding suggests.

facts.install: Docker image or Docker Compose; Kubernetes is also supported
facts.engines: Model-agnostic; the agent builder supports bring-your-own AI provider credentials
facts.dataFormat: Built-in app data and app definitions are stored in CouchDB, files in MinIO/S3-compatible object storage, and connected external data remains in its source system
facts.gapVsPaid: Budibase is oriented toward internal teams, making public portals, external-user onboarding, and managed customer-facing deployment less seamless than Knack.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires Docker and persistent storage; production use also means owning upgrades, TLS, backups, and database/network access

alternatives.name: NocoBase
alternatives.desc: A database-backed app builder with pages, forms, roles, workflows, and enough plugins to become your next maintenance hobby.

facts.install: NocoBase CLI or Docker deployment with MySQL, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL
facts.engines: Built-in AI employees can connect to common LLMs; exact provider support depends on installed AI plugins
facts.dataFormat: Business data lives in standard relational tables in the configured MySQL, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL database; files use configured local or object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It requires self-hosting and exposes more database machinery, while Knack makes a small hosted customer portal much easier to publish and operate.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires a database, secrets, and deployment administration; the community license also preserves NocoBase branding and restricts some uses

alternatives.name: REI3
alternatives.desc: A sober business-app builder with forms, reports, roles, workflows, and no per-user meter.

facts.install: Native Linux/Windows server package or Docker Compose, connected to PostgreSQL
facts.dataFormat: Human-readable application records and configuration live in a PostgreSQL database controlled by the operator
facts.gapVsPaid: Its utilitarian self-hosted business interfaces are less polished for branded external portals and nontechnical customer access than Knack.
facts.setupBlocker: You must provision PostgreSQL and configure a server/reverse proxy; it is not a managed one-click workspace

alternatives.name: Softr Free
alternatives.desc: A hosted portal builder with pages, forms, record editing, user groups, and visibility rules on the free plan.

facts.dataFormat: App definitions and any Softr Database records live in Softr's cloud; connected-source records remain in the external source, with Softr proxying requests and caching data for up to 24 hours; table blocks can export CSV or XLSX
facts.gapVsPaid: The free plan cannot reproduce a production Knack portal without visible Softr branding and plan limits on users, records, and advanced permissions.
facts.setupBlocker: No software install; the first hurdle is choosing and authenticating a data source, then mapping its fields and permissions

rejectedAlternatives.name: Saltcorn
rejectedAlternatives.desc: It does the job, but its own security page lists fresh critical RCE, SQL injection, path-traversal, and cross-tenant bugs.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Starter plan and a small-team structured database DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Knack in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: model structured records in a small self-hosted database app, provide grid, form, kanban, and role-based filtered views, and expose a documented API.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create workspaces, bases, tables, fields, records, attachments, relations, and saved views.
Support text, number, currency, date, boolean, select, formula-lite, and relation field types.
Build grid, form, kanban, and record-detail views from one canonical schema.
Add role-based permissions, optimistic concurrency checks, audit history, and trash restore.
Provide CSV import or export and a token-authenticated REST API generated from the schema.
Ship migrations, seed data, backups, health checks, and a schema export format.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out full spreadsheet formula compatibility.
Deliberately leave out hundreds of automations and integrations.
Deliberately leave out large-enterprise governance and vendor-managed scale.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
